messages:
maya: Heads-up — running into an OPA/Conftest reject during CI on a terraform change. Seems the change that pins the provider source in a nested module is tripping the policy that blocks implicit provider sources. Plan is blocked in premerge. Any quick ideas?

oscar: Can you paste the exact error? Might be the new constraint `required_providers` vs implicit module providers.

maya: Error from CI: 
```
Error: OPA policy 'no-implicit-provider' violated
module.foo: provider source must be explicit, found legacy provider declaration
Policy: /policies/terraform/no-implicit-provider.rego
```

liam: Ah yeah — we tightened that policy last week for compliance. It flags modules that use implicit hashicorp providers (eg. provider "aws" with no source). If this is a nested module you need to update module's registry reference or add a `providers` map in the root module.

anika: Reminder: we're inside the freeze window through EOD for the US-west region. If this is a non-security rollback we need an approvals exemption from the change-freeze channel. @ops-approvals-bot will require risk doc + owner.

maya: This is just making module source explicit — low risk. But the plan also shows a helm release reconcile that failed earlier today due to chart propagation lag. Might need a small manual sync after the terraform apply. I can prepare the risk note.

infra-bot: OPA scan result posted to the PR — https://ci.internal/reports/1245 
(reacted with :warning:)

oscar: If it's truly low risk we can request a freeze-exemption. @sophie can you do the quick repo review? Want another set of eyes on module source change.

sophie: On it. Quick checklist: 1) confirm module registry source is canonical 2) ensure provider constraints are compatible with Dedicated infra (nv6 GPU pools) 3) smoke plan for drift.

maya: Pasting the relevant terraform snippet: 
```hcl
module "training_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-infra/gcp-gpu-modules.git//training?ref=v2.1.0"
  providers = { google = google } 
}

# previously module referenced without explicit source, which triggered the policy
```

liam: Two practical fixes: 1) update the module to include explicit `required_providers` and bump ref, or 2) if module is external, add a policy-exemption PR referencing the change and a short justification. Given freeze window, option 2 with minimal blast radius is faster.

anika: Ops-approvals-bot requires: (a) owner, (b) risk summary, (c) rollback plan, (d) duration of exemption. Keep it under 2 hours if possible.

maya: Drafting exemption: "Low-risk module source pin to satisfy OPA. No infra scaling, only module metadata. Owner: maya. Rollback: revert PR. Exemption duration: 1 hour." Will post in 5.

oscar: Also check downstream helm release reconcile — if image tags are unchanged should be fine. If charts changed we might trigger a redeploy. Quick way: `kubectl rollout status` after sync.

maya: Filed exemption request: https://ops.internal/exemptions/9876 — tagged @ops-approvals-bot and linked the PR.

ops-approvals-bot: Exemption request 9876 created. Please add risk doc link and mark owner field. Approvals required: 1 infra lead + SRE.

sophie: Reviewed the diff, LGTM aside from updating module README to note explicit provider requirement. Small nit.

liam: If approvals come through, I'll do an on-call watch during apply and run the helm manual sync if reconcile lags.

maya: Approval granted by infra lead, SRE pending (pinged). Applying once SRE signs.

infra-bot: CI pipeline: policy checks -> terraform plan -> helm diff. Current status: policy checks failed -> waiting on exemption.

maya: SRE signed off. Proceeding with apply in 5. Will monitor nv6 pools and helm controllers.

oscar: Thanks — I'll be ready to assist with any manual kube syncs.

maya: Apply done, plan output: 
```
Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.
No infra changes besides metadata pins.
```

sophie: Nice. I'll follow up with a tiny docs PR noting how module consumers should pin providers to avoid future OPA hits.

liam: Helm reconcile lag resolved after manual sync `flux reconcile helmrelease training --namespace infra`. All good.

maya: Closing thread — exemption will be recorded. Thanks all :tada:
